### Contributing guidelines - [x] I have read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) - [x] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) - [x] I have updated 'mini.nvim' to latest version of the `main` branch ### Module(s) mini.git ### Neovim version 0.12.x ### Description I'm a very heavy user of `mini.git`, wonderful package. One thing I have noticed, is that [CTRL-W T](https://neovim.io/doc/user/windows/#CTRL-W_T) doesn't work on buffers created by mini.git. What I like to do, is use a combination of `:Git log %` and `MiniGit.show_at_cursor()` to split the window with log in one side, and the other with basically the output of `git show `. Very often I end up using `MiniGit.show_diff_source()`, and sometimes I end up with multiple splits, at which point it becomes unreadable, so ideally, I would like to send one of those splits to a new tab, and this is where I noticed that `CTRL-W T` doesn't work. As a reference, this what I sometimes end up with, or even more: What actually happens when I press `CTRL-W T` is that the window disappears. As a workaround, `:tab split` does work, but the difference with `CTRL-W T` is it leaves the original window, and what I actually want is to *move* the window to a new tab, just like `CTRL-W T` does. ### Reproduction 1. Create separate 'nvim-repro' config directory: - '~/.config/nvim-repro/' on Unix - '~/AppData/Local/nvim-repro/' on Windows 2. Inside 'nvim-repro' directory create a file named 'init.lua'. Populate it with the following content: ```lua vim.pack.add { { src = "https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim" }, } require"mini.git".setup() ``` 3. Run `NVIM_APPNAME=nvim-repro nvim` (i.e. execute `nvim` with `NVIM_APPNAME` environment variable set to "nvim-repro"). Wait for all dependencies to install. 4. Open nvim in a git repo 5. Open nvim and run a command like `vert Git log --oneline %`. (% for current buffer, or replace with a filepath) 6. Now try to send the window to a new tab with `CTRL-W T` and the result will be that it just closes the window. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2bd6fa7a-9f95-46a9-b31f-b1da78eb2abb
What to do after reporting an issue After reporting the issue, it is safe (and even recommended for cleaner possible future bug reports) to remove 'nvim-repro' config from the system: - Delete config directory ('~/.config/nvim-repro' on Unix). - Delete data directory ('~/.local/share/nvim-repro' on Unix). - Delete state directory ('~/.local/state/nvim-repro' on Unix).

comment_data.body:
Thanks for the issue!

This is kind of by design because 'mini.git' does the buffer cleanup after closing the window. Doing `<C-w>T` seems to act like "open new window in tabpage and close this window".

Not doing cleanup would result in multiple (hidden) stale buffers after just closing the window that showed it. The `bufhidden=wipe` would fix it, but it would result in deleting the `minigit` buffer if other buffer is shown in that window.

The current solution on the user side is to do `MiniGit.show_at_cursor({ split = 'tab' })` to force showing the info in the new tabpage. This requires a bit of a foresight, but seems okay.

I'll take a look if it can be solved in 'mini.git'. Probably a check to not force delete the buffer if it is shown in some other window would be enough.

@echasnovski,

I was also investigating, so here is my take:

```diff

diff --git a/lua/mini/git.lua b/lua/mini/git.lua
index 6740d977..63ad62c2 100644
--- a/lua/mini/git.lua
+++ b/lua/mini/git.lua
@@ -1156,6 +1156,7 @@ end
 H.define_minigit_window = function(cleanup)
   local buf_id, win_id = vim.api.nvim_get_current_buf(), vim.api.nvim_get_current_win()
   vim.bo.swapfile, vim.bo.buflisted = false, false
+  vim.bo.bufhidden = 'hide'
 
   -- Define action to finish editing Git related file
   local finish_au_id
@@ -1170,7 +1171,7 @@ H.define_minigit_window = function(cleanup)
     if vim.is_callable(cleanup) then vim.schedule(cleanup) end
   end
   -- - Use `nested` to allow other events (`WinEnter` for 'mini.statusline')
-  local events = { 'WinClosed', 'BufDelete', 'BufWipeout', 'VimLeave' }
+  local events = { 'BufHidden', 'BufDelete', 'BufWipeout', 'VimLeave' }
   local opts = { nested = true, callback = finish, desc = 'Cleanup window and buffer' }
   finish_au_id = vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd(events, opts)
 end
diff --git a/tests/test_git.lua b/tests/test_git.lua
index 14ce77e9..34932536 100644
--- a/tests/test_git.lua
+++ b/tests/test_git.lua
@@ -2593,7 +2593,6 @@ T[':Git']['output']['defines proper window/buffer cleanup'] = function()
   child.lua([[table.insert(_G.stdio_queue, { { 'out', 'World' } })]])
   child.cmd('vertical Git log')
   local buf_id_2, win_id_2 = get_buf(), get_win()
-  set_buf(new_scratch_buf())
   eq(#child.api.nvim_tabpage_list_wins(0), 2)
   child.api.nvim_buf_delete(buf_id_2, { force = true })
   eq(#child.api.nvim_tabpage_list_wins(0), 1)

```

> ```diff
> diff --git a/tests/test_git.lua b/tests/test_git.lua
> index 14ce77e9..34932536 100644
> --- a/tests/test_git.lua
> +++ b/tests/test_git.lua
> @@ -2593,7 +2593,6 @@ T[':Git']['output']['defines proper window/buffer cleanup'] = function()
>    child.lua([[table.insert(_G.stdio_queue, { { 'out', 'World' } })]])
>    child.cmd('vertical Git log')
>    local buf_id_2, win_id_2 = get_buf(), get_win()
> -  set_buf(new_scratch_buf())
>    eq(#child.api.nvim_tabpage_list_wins(0), 2)
>    child.api.nvim_buf_delete(buf_id_2, { force = true })
>    eq(#child.api.nvim_tabpage_list_wins(0), 1)
> ```

This is testing a relevant behavior that is described in its comment: "Should close window when buffer is deleted". I.e. manually deleting the buffer should also close the window that was created for it.

I have a solution that works (delete buffer in the cleanup only if it is not shown anywhere), but I'll take wondering if using `winfixbuf` here is a more proper solution. This would simplify the logic, but would not allow switching the buffer in the dedicated windows, though.

Should now be resolved on the latest `main`. But I'll probably look into making all custom windows that show custom buffers have 'winfixbuf' enabled. This would mean that changing buffers from such windows will be not intended, but that is probably the good behavior (showing other buffer would require an extra split).
